gap: No result ChatGPT got lists the cheapest LTE-only camera in the category: Arenti sells its GO3G (2K pan-tilt, SIM included, no Wi-Fi) for $39.99 on arenti.com today (2026-11-14). That is less than ChatGPT's cheapest card (eco4life, $49.69), about a third of its Reolink Go PT Plus 'budget' card ($122.94), and about a sixth of the eufy S330 at $249.99 on eufy.com.
standout_why: I compared against four pages. homesecurityradar.com/guides/lte-security-camera-data-cost (cited) has Reolink plan prices, 3-year totals for Reolink Go Ultra and Arlo Go 2, and 'No published price found' for the eufy S330 data plan. homesecurityradar.com/guides/security-cameras-without-wifi lists eufy S330 at $249.99, Go PT Ultra at $229.99, several Reolink Go models, Arlo Go 2 at $159.99 and some PoE cameras. smarthomeexplorer.com covers Reolink Go PT Ultra, eufy S330, Arlo Go 2 and a sponsored Waggle, with prices that contradict each other within the page. securitycamlab.com/best/best-cellular-security-camera covers Go PT Ultra, S330, Vosker V300, Arlo Go 2 and Go Plus, with no plan prices. None of them lists the Arenti GO3G or any LTE-only camera under $89.99. smarthomeexplorer also says the Reolink Go PT Ultra SIM works on AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. Reolink's own spec list names only T-Mobile and AT&T (prepaid data only), plus FreedomPop and Mint.
decides: This confirms the Arenti GO3G as our budget pick and moves it up: at $39.99 it undercuts every camera ChatGPT showed. eufy S330 ($249.99) stays the pick for Verizon-only areas or anyone who wants Wi-Fi fallback, because it is the only camera here whose maker page lists all three US carriers and a Wi-Fi mode. Reolink Go PT Ultra and Go PT Plus lose on carriers for Verizon-only sites: Reolink's US spec list names T-Mobile and AT&T prepaid only, and the cameras have no Wi-Fi. Arlo Go 2 needs a SIM bought separately (per homesecurityradar), and our page records an Arlo Secure subscription requirement.
